testing_gaps: Apps/App/tests/WaterCompositionChecks.h:109-120 exercises absent, empty-seed and disabled water with visible single particles, while SecondGroupTests verifies active fluid depth/resolve and BistroAdditionsTests verifies visible water. There is still no isolated pixel oracle with active water and transparent mesh geometry on both sides of the water surface; swapped Far/Near routing would not be directly diagnosed by those existing assertions. This is an acknowledged acceptance limit in docs/reports/2026-11-05-app-render-pipelines-validation.md:210-213. The integration report also acknowledges this limit.

Apps/App/tests/BistroRenderGraphTests.cpp:121-146 intentionally removes particle drawing, nonzero transparent contribution and the authored coplanar masked plate overlay from the exact pooled/dedicated HDR oracle, then restores them at lines 208-215 before resize/SR smoke. Thus the successful byte-equality matrix does not independently establish pooled/dedicated equality for nonzero transparent or particle contribution; separate composition/pixel tests and restored ordinary-rendering validation cover their behavior without that equality comparison. A deterministic single-contributor pooling case would close this specific coverage boundary.

No baseline/candidate CPU graph-recording or GPU frame-time comparison establishes the cost of the integrated prepared-view topology. BistroRenderPipeline.cpp:206-215 creates mesh, expansion and consumer jobs per view/patch; GDX12RenderGraph.cpp:400 queries accesses per job; GDX12GrassRenderer.cpp:644-645 supplies every prepared output constant to each grass consumer, while FindOutput at lines 434-439 searches outputs linearly. These are concrete profiling targets at the documented 4,620-node Bistro topology, but source inspection and passing functional tests do not establish a consequential regression or speedup.

The supplied acceptance evidence exercises the primary RTX 3060 Laptop GPU. No second-GPU allocation or frame-time measurement is available; the largest-patch shared arena and its maximum-capacity allocation test do not establish performance on other hardware. This reviewer performed source inspection only and did not rerun builds, GPU tests or timings.
